title: Declarative typed parsers and fallback profiles — SDK PRD (scratch)
content:
Context and motivation:

This is a working PRD exploring a developer-friendly approach to producing reliable structured output and resilient tool-calling in incremental/streaming calls. Many teams have asked for stronger guarantees about the shape of responses when using hosted streaming APIs (progressive outputs, tool triggers, JSON blocks). The problem space is twofold: (1) parsers in client code are brittle when partial or malformed frames are emitted mid-stream, and (2) fallback and resume behavior across network/SDK boundaries is ad-hoc and hard to reason about for product engineers.

Our proposal centers on two complementary primitives: a small declarative "typed parser" language that annotates expected structured segments in the stream, and a compact per-session fallback profile token that encodes developer-declared recovery semantics. Together they surface a clear contract between server streaming behavior and client SDKs so that incremental validation, graceful degradation, and reproducible tool-call handoffs are practical without heavy client-side state machines.

Goals (measurable):
- Reduce client-side parsing errors for incremental structured output by 60% on integration tests (defined by downstream SDK test suite)
- Enable safe tool-calls over streaming with deterministic retry semantics in >= 90% of observed failure modes in canary apps
- Keep added bytes for parser hints and fallback token under 1% of average payload size for typical chat-with-tools flows
- Produce ergonomics that let a developer wire typed parsers with one line of SDK config in common languages (JS/TS, Python, Go)

Non-goals:
- We are not introducing a full schema language or runtime SDk-based validation engine for arbitrary models. This is intentionally minimal: a typed fragment descriptor + optional example-driven assertions.
- This PRD does not address long-term storage of session artifacts or audit logs beyond integrating with existing Console telemetry and trace ids.

User stories:
- As an SDK user, I want to declare that the stream will contain a sequence of frames where some frames are JSON objects labelled "action" with keys [name, args], so my frontend can render progressive UI updates without fragile regex parsing.
- As a backend engineer integrating tool calls, I want deterministic retry: if a tool-call frame failed due to a transient network error, the client can request a resume token and the server will either re-emit a final resolved tool result or provide a compatible fallback summary.
- As a platform PM, I want to show in Console the percentage of sessions that used typed-parsers and the frequency of fallback activations so we can prioritize improvements.

Design proposal (high level):
1) Typed Parser Fragments
- Small declarative fragment spec emitted as the first meta-frame of a session or as an explicit header in a streaming chunk.
- Syntax is intentionally tiny: sequence of named frames, each frame contains: name, expected mime (e.g., application/json), optional minimal schema hints (flat key types: string|number|boolean|object), and a "commit" policy (instant | final | checkpointable). Example (pseudo):
  frames: [ {name: action, mime: application/json, keys: {name: string, args: object}, commit: checkpointable}, {name: narrative, mime: text/plain, commit: final} ]
- Parsers in SDKs map these frames to typed callbacks and provide helpers to accept progressive partial JSON (e.g., emit partial tokens but only call the typed callback for well-formed objects).

2) Fallback Profile Token (compact)
- An opaque base64 token emitted once per session describing client-visible fallback policies: idempotency-key, max-retries, fallback-mode (summarize|best-effort|abort-to-default), and preferred alternative model or variant.
- Server and SDK share a small deterministic protocol for resume: if connection is lost, client resubmits resume request with token; server checks whether it can continue from existing model state or must emit a summarized fallback.
- Token intentionally small (<= 256 bytes) and signed by Redwood control plane to prevent tampering.

3) SDK Ergonomics
- Binding patterns: onSessionStart(options) where options.typedParsers and options.fallbackProfile are optional. Minimal example (JS):
  const s = Redwood.stream({model: 'rwd-chat-mini', typedParsers: parserSpec, fallbackProfile: 'rwd-fp:...'});
  s.on('frame:action', (obj) => renderAction(obj));
  s.on('frame:narrative', (chunk) => appendText(chunk));
- Progressive validation helpers: sdk.validateFrame(frameName, rawPayload) -> {status: ok|partial|invalid, parsed?:object, issues?: [string]}. SDK will surface partial status so apps can show loading indicators until commit policy is satisfied.
- Retry/resume helper: sdk.resume(sessionToken) abstracts server handshake and returns either continued stream or final fallback event.

4) Server behavior and compatibility
- If a typed parser spec is present, server tries to prefer emitting clearly delimited frames. For models that cannot guarantee exact structure, server will emit frame candidates and attach a confidence tag; SDKs will surface confidence so clients can choose to wait for commit policy or show provisional UI.
- Backwards compatibility: all typed parser and fallback metadata are optional and carried in meta-frames (non-breaking). Older SDKs ignore meta-frames; newer SDKs opt-in.

Operational considerations
- Telemetry: record typed-parser adoption per app, fallback activations, resume success rate, and per-frame parse error counts. Add lightweight counters used by Console dashboards.
- Cost impact: minimal. Meta-frames are small, but we will measure token overhead on high-volume flows.
- Security: fallback tokens must be signed/scheme-checked. Tool-calls continue to follow existing authorization flows; parser hints do not expose PII unless the caller includes it explicitly.

Rollout plan (phased):
- Phase 0 (experiment): internal SDK + canary apps (start with solutions-engineering demo apps) — implement parser spec emission and SDK-side validateFrame helper. Duration 4 weeks.
- Phase 1 (beta): public SDK opt-in and Console telemetry. Document API patterns. Duration 6 weeks.
- Phase 2 (GA): default availability with graceful server-side heuristics for model variants. Offer migration guide. Duration 8 weeks.

Acceptance criteria:
- SDKs (JS, Python) ship validateFrame and resume helpers with unit tests covering partial/malformed frames.
- Integration tests: 95% pass rate on simulated flaky network with resume token semantics validated.
- Console shows adoption and fallback activation metrics for beta customers.

Open questions and tradeoffs:
- How expressive should schema hints be? Flat key types preserve simplicity but limit complex nested validation. We should start minimal and iterate.
- Should the fallback token be stateless (opaque signed) or server-held? Opaque token is simpler for scale but harder to revoke mid-session.
- How to represent confidence and partial tokens without bloating the streaming path? Consider numeric confidence + categorical reasons.

Implementation notes (initial work items):
- proto: meta-frame wire format and compact typed parser JSON schema (backend + runtime)
- sdk: validateFrame, typed frame event routing, resume() helper, and example app for tools demo
- server: meta-frame parsing, checkpointable emission mode, fallback token signer, and resume endpoint
- console: simple dashboard tiles and traces for typed-parser sessions and fallback rates

Related artifacts and references:
- Demo app: solutions-engineering/stream-tools-demo (TBD)
- Confluence prod note: PROD-142 (linked)
- Jira epic: JIRA-3214

Notes to reviewers (quick):
- This draft focuses on the developer ergonomics of making streaming structured output reliable for client apps and tool-call patterns. Look especially at the minimal parser syntax and the resume/fallback tradeoffs.
- Feedback sought: an example of how a mobile SDK might render partial JSON objects in constrained memory, and whether a server-held resume pointer is required for enterprise customers with stricter audit needs.

-- end of scratch PRD --
